newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - PUBLIC SUPPORTS NATO, EU BIDS - POLL.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - PUBLIC SUPPORTS NATO, EU BIDS - POLL.

text.p: A recent survey conducted by Lithuanian pollster Vilmorus found fairly strong public support for the country's bid to join NATO and the European Union (EU), parliament's public relations department said on Tuesday.
The public relations department said in a statement that 48.9 percent of those polled backed the country's efforts to join the EU while 47.7 percent wanted to see Lithuania in NATO.
The respondents were asked how they would vote if referenda were held on the issues tomorrow.
The poll questioned 1,000 people between the ages of 18 and 74 and was conducted the week of February 7 to 11.
Of those surveyed, 10.6 percent said they were opposed to EU membership while 14.2 percent said they would vote against joining NATO.
Many of the respondents were undecided, with 32.6 percent saying they were unsure how they would vote in a referendum on EU membership and 29.6 percent saying the same about NATO.
Eight percent said they would not bother to cast a ballot in a vote on joining the 15-member EU while 8.5 percent said they would not come out for a referendum on NATO.
The public relations department said that "NATO membership is mostly opposed by Russians," while most of the opposition to joining the EU came from rural respondents.
Joining both organisations is the top foreign policy priority of the government.

Diplomats and analysts say that Lithuania's long-term prospects for EU membership look good but have all bit written it and Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia out of the first round of NATO expansion.
Russia has strong objections to NATO membership and is especially hostile to the idea of the Baltic countries joining its old Cold-War foe.
